disease_label_per_paper: Immunoglobulin G4-related disease: probable type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis at initial presentation with spontaneous remission, relapsing 2.5 years later as IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
presentation_phase_note: Structured presentation = the initial presentation (Day 1: epigastric pain, Day-1 labs and Day-1 abdominal MRI). The Month-32 relapse (IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis) is kept as non-ranking clinical course.
presentation_summary: 46-year-old Japanese man presented on Day 1 with epigastric pain that had started six days earlier; no significant past medical history, occasional drinker only, no regular medications/OTC/herbal supplements.

Day-1 labs: amylase 173 U/L, lipase 485 U/L; normal hepatobiliary enzymes (AST 16, ALT 14, ALP 67, GGT 30 U/L, total bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL); total protein 7.6 g/dL, albumin 4.6 g/dL, WBC 7.5 x10^3/uL, CRP 0.21 mg/dL.
Day-1 abdominal MRI: 4 x 2 cm mass in the pancreatic body with high DWI signal and low ADC, mild dilation of the distal main pancreatic duct.

risk_context.source_text_value: He had no history of habitual alcohol consumption (occasional drinker only)
was not taking any regular medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements prior to presentation

He had no significant past medical history other than having received a two-dose primary series of an unspecified COVID-19 messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine (approximately 19 and 18 months prior to Day 1).

confirmatory_findings.finding: Serum IgG4 elevated at 224.0 mg/dL (1.85 x ULN) on Day 1
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The serum IgG4 level was elevated at 224.0 mg/dL (1.85 times the upper limit of normal (ULN; 121 mg/dL)).
confirmatory_findings.note: Disease-defining serologic criterion (ICDC Level 2 serology); kept non-ranking.

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Serological screening for viral hepatitis (hepatitis B surface antigen and anti-hepatitis C virus antibody) was negative.

confirmatory_findings.finding: EUS-FNA (Day 21): Class II cytology, benign inflammatory changes with mature lymphocytes and plasma cells, negative for malignancy
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) was performed primarily to rule out malignancy, yielding Class II cytology (benign inflammatory changes with mature lymphocytes and plasma cells, negative for malignancy)

confirmatory_findings.finding: Clinical diagnosis of probable type 1 AIP (ICDC Level 2 parenchymal imaging + Level 2 serology; Japanese 2018 criteria)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: a clinical diagnosis of AIP (probable Type 1 AIP) was established

clinical_course_events.finding: Spontaneous clinical and radiological remission by Month 3 without immunosuppression (Day 90: amylase 85 U/L, lipase 82 U/L, CRP 0.02 mg/dL)
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: By Month 3, his clinical symptoms and repeat abdominal imaging findings had resolved, and his pancreatic enzyme levels had nearly normalized (lipase mildly elevated at 82 U/L)

clinical_course_events.finding: Relapse at Month 32 as IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis: GGT 1569 U/L, ALP 261 U/L, AST 110 U/L, ALT 172 U/L, IgG 2155 mg/dL, IgG4 573 mg/dL; CT bile duct wall thickening; MRCP multiple smooth intrahepatic/extrahepatic strictures
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: his laboratory evaluation revealed ... a markedly elevated GGT level (1,569 U/L) juxtaposed with a disproportionately low ALP level (261 U/L). Transaminases were also elevated (aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 110 U/L, ALT 172 U/L). Additionally, his serum total IgG level was elevated at 2,155 mg/dL, and his serum IgG4 level was markedly elevated at 573.0 mg/dL

actual_treatment: Initial episode: conservative management without immunosuppression
Relapse: oral prednisolone 40 mg/day with prophylactic TMP-SMX (later stopped for suspected drug-induced liver injury)

outcome.source_text_value: Coupled with normalized transaminases, normal IgG levels, and symptom resolution, the patient achieved and maintained clinical remission.

quality_warnings: No vital signs were reported at the Day-1 presentation.
Serum IgG4 (disease-defining serology), EUS-FNA cytology, and the paper's clinical diagnosis are kept non-ranking.
The Month-32 relapse presentation (IgG4-SC) is not used as the presentation snapshot because its history includes the prior autoimmune pancreatitis diagnosis.
CRP converted from mg/dL to mg/L (x10); WBC x10^3/uL = x10^9/L.
